description: You are given n balloons indexed 0 to n-1, each with a number. When you burst balloon i, you gain nums[i-1]*nums[i]*nums[i+1] coins. Find the maximum coins you can collect by bursting all balloons. Boundary balloons have value 1.
intuition: The key insight is thinking backwards: instead of which balloon to burst first, think about which balloon to burst LAST in each interval. The last balloon sees the interval boundaries as its neighbors, making the subproblems independent.
approach: Use interval DP. Think of the last balloon to burst in each interval. dp[i][j] = max coins from bursting all balloons between i and j (exclusive). For each possible last balloon k in (i,j), dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + nums[i]*nums[k]*nums[j]).
explanation:
1. Pad nums with 1 on both sides to handle boundary conditions.
2. dp[i][j] = max coins from bursting all balloons strictly between i and j.
3. For each interval length, try each balloon k as the LAST to burst in that interval.
4. Cost of bursting k last = nums[i]*nums[k]*nums[j] (boundaries remain).
5. Total = dp[i][k] + dp[k][j] + that cost.
hints: Think about which balloon you burst LAST in a subarray.
The key insight is that the last balloon in an interval sees the interval boundaries as neighbors.
Pad the array with 1s at both ends to simplify boundary handling.

phases.label: For each interval, try each last balloon

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: There are O(n²) boundary pairs and up to n choices of lastBurst per pair. DP lookups make the work per choice constant.

complexityVariables.n: Number of original balloons, excluding the two boundary values added by the algorithm.
